$comment: Correctness and repeated-run stability are gated on every benchmark run.
Relative performance budgets are evaluated only when --baseline points to a
report with the same corpus hash, implementation, OS, architecture, Node major,
and CPU model. This prevents results from unlike machines becoming a false gate.
Absolute budgets need no baseline, so they are the class that actually gates a
pull request. Their thresholds are deliberately generous against measured
values so a loaded or shared runner cannot flake them; tight regression
detection remains the job of the relative lane against a compatible baseline.
columnar.data-plane.million-feature was measured on a shared linux host while
two other build agents ran, deliberately including its heaviest contention:
20.00 backing bytes/feature (deterministic — the packed fixture is 8 + 4 + 4 + 4
bytes/row), 20.0-35.8 peak retained bytes/feature, and a median throughput
between 2,154,706 and 8,776,756 features/second for the complete build + worker
round trip + deck.gl binding pipeline over 1,000,000 rows.
The ceilings and floor below sit 1.2x, 4.5x, and 4.3x clear of the worst of
those observations, so contention cannot flake them. They still gate real
regressions: a per-feature JavaScript object result for the same fixture costs
300+ bytes/feature and an order of magnitude less throughput, and any payload
copy reintroduced into the transfer or projection path fails the scenario's
zero-copy invariant outright rather than merely slowing it down.
columnar.aggregate.million-row (honua-io/honua-sdk-js#939) reduces 1,000,000
GeoArrow rows to 1,024 groups with a count-plus-sum metric set. The two
failure thresholds below are the numbers the issue itself names: 8 retained
bytes/input row and a 2,000,000 input rows/second floor. Measured on the same
shared linux host: 0.2246-0.2434 retained bytes/input row and 9,002,553-
14,196,335 input rows/second across five repetitions, so the ceiling sits 33x
and the floor 4.5x clear of the worst reading. retainedBytesPerInputRow is a
peak of live bytes sampled after a forced collection at each scan checkpoint,
not an allocation-rate delta; the harness fails the scenario outright when no
collector is exposed. It still catches the regression it exists for: decoding
rows into objects before reducing them costs hundreds of bytes/input row and
would hold them live at exactly those checkpoints. outputBackingBytesPerGroup
is deterministic at 32.25 (a utf8 group key plus two float64 metric columns)
and states the property the whole issue turns on — the result is sized by the
group count, not the row count.
columnar.result.bounded-window (honua-io/honua-sdk-js#942) converts a 1,000-row
window out of a 1,000,000-row GeoArrow batch into object-shaped features. The
two failure thresholds are the numbers the issue itself names: NFR-001's 1 MB
per 1,000 converted features is exactly 1,024 retained bytes/feature, and
NFR-002 sets a 200,000 features/second floor. Measured on the same shared linux
host across twenty samples spanning a quiet host and one running three other
build agents: 219.0-258.6 retained bytes/feature and per-run median throughput
between 748,842 and 1,517,304 features/second. The ceiling therefore sits 4.0x
and the floor 3.7x clear of the worst measured median, and the advisory warning
sits below the loaded-host median so contention alone cannot raise it.
Throughput is timed over twenty-five consecutive distinct windows rather than
one: a single bounded conversion is milliseconds of work, short enough that one
collection landing inside it swings the reading by tens of percent and trips the
lab's repeated-run variability check on noise. Consecutive distinct windows are
the paging workload an application actually performs, so this costs no honesty;
converting one window repeatedly would instead have flattered the number out of
warm cache. retainedBytesPerFeature still measures exactly one window, which is
the quantity NFR-001 bounds.
retainedBytesPerFeature is a live-bytes reading taken after a forced collection
with the converted window still held, not an allocation-rate delta, so it
measures what the window actually retains beyond the batch backings it was cut
from; the harness fails the scenario outright when no collector is exposed. The
throughput floor is what catches the regression that matters here: the window
is one thousandth of the batch, so any implementation that reverted to scanning
or validating the whole batch per conversion would miss the floor by orders of
magnitude while still returning the correct thousand features.
columnar.batch-cache.million-row-round-trip carries the persistence NFRs of
honua-io/honua-sdk-js#940: serialize plus deserialize of a 1,000,000-row packed
GeoArrow fixture (16,000,000 backing bytes). Measured on the same shared linux
host, with other build agents active: 1.3334 envelope bytes per backing byte
(deterministic — base64 is 1.3333 and the envelope's own JSON adds 0.0001),
53.35-53.39 live retained bytes/row, and 689,528-714,447 rows/second.
The ceilings below are the issue's own limits rather than measured-plus-margin,
because two of the three are deterministic: the envelope ratio has zero
variance and retained bytes vary by 0.03%, so a 1.5x-clear ceiling would gate
nothing. The rows/second floor is 2.7x under the worst observed run, which is
the only metric contention can move.
